text:
Sam (CS): FYI, customer (Acme) reports duplicated tokens and a truncated final chunk when their client reconnects quickly after an auth refresh.
Priya (Eng): Can you paste logs + example session headers? :eyes:
Sam (CS): Repro steps I ran:
1) open SSE stream -> get partial output
2) rotate token (they do KMS auto-rotate)
3) client reconnects within ~150ms using new token
Observed: server sent final chunk twice and billing showed 2 generation charges.
Here's the minimal reproduction they used:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -N "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-3x" \
# client reads partial, then disconnects and reconnects with new token quickly
```
Client then reconnects quickly with new token header (no Last-Event-ID).
Jordan (SRE): Any proxy in front? We've seen sticky connections (Fastly) cause delayed acks before; could be related.
Sam (CS): Customer is on hosted API (us-east), no custom proxy. They quoted request id `req_01F8X` in their support ticket.
Priya (Eng): Priya here — our resume path uses session_id + offset. If token rotates mid-stream we create a new auth context but the resume code tries to reattach using seqnum; that can cause the server to replay the last chunk if the ack window is ambiguous.
Alice (Platform): Do we tie billing to session id or a generation id? Billing should dedupe by generation_id if present.
BillingBot: Billing alert: duplicate charge detected for invoice 0xA34 referencing req_01F8X
Sam (CS): Server snippets (redacted):
```
[2025-11-03T12:34:56Z] session resume attempt: session=abc123 offset=42 from=client
[2025-11-03T12:34:56Z] output chunk id=chunk_987 seq=42 sent
[2025-11-03T12:34:56Z] reconnect new_auth: token rotated, old session orphaned
[2025-11-03T12:34:56Z] resume fallback: replaying last chunk to ensure continuity
```
Priya (Eng): Hypothesis: when token rotates we orphan the old session but the client reconnects with the same session header; our resume code double-sends the last incomplete chunk while also starting a fresh generation. Fixes: a) make resume idempotent wrt generation_id; b) treat token rotation as a resume-break unless client sends explicit resume token.
Jordan (SRE): Quick check — can we confirm the client did not send `Last-Event-ID`? If it's missing our heuristics might assume missing ack and replay.
Sam (CS): Customer confirms their library did not send Last-Event-ID on reconnect. They expected resume to be transparent.
Priya (Eng): Action items:
- Eng: add server-side dedupe by generation_id and treat duplicate chunk ids as no-op (will open PR).
- Platform: document that token rotation can break transparent resume; add SDK helper to persist resume token across auth rotations.
- CS: offer credits for duplicated charge and coordinate test with customer.
Jordan (SRE): Short-term mitigation: if reconnect occurs within 1s and token changed, prefer failing resume with an explicit error (so client can restart) instead of replaying chunk.
Priya (Eng): Agree. I'll spin up a branch and include extended logging to capture generation_id + chunk id for future triage.
Sam (CS): I'll open the support ticket, include repro steps, and request consent to issue a credit.
Priya (Eng): PR opened: `fix/sse-resume-dedupe-2025` — contains dedupe by chunk id + generation_id and a guard for token-rotation resume.
Sam (CS): Customer tested patched flow + server-side fix; confirms duplicate final chunk and duplicate billing no longer occur. :white_check_mark: 
Sam (CS): Closing loop here — will follow up with postmortem if we see recurrence.
